links.targetTitle: Spark Savings v2 instances bound risk with a supply cap and
An L2 savings vault gains a bridge operation as a rate-limit

title: The operations that pull user deposits out of the savings vaults carry no rate limit at all
content:
Under each Savings instance's risk parameters sits a second `Rate Limits` block covering "this conduit's take and transferAssets operations" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.9.1.4.2.2). For all three products both are unbounded: "The take rate limits are: `maxAmount`: Unlimited" and "The transferAssets rate limits are: `maxAmount`: Unlimited" (.9.1.4.2.3/.4, .9.2.4.2.3/.4, .9.3.4.2.3/.4).

These are the operations that move deposited assets from the vault into Spark's operational control — the point at which user funds become deployable. Making them unlimited means the entire deposit base of a product can be drawn in a single action, with no per-day regeneration curve slowing it.

Seen from the asset-allocation side this is consistent: elsewhere the Artifact leaves unbounded whichever direction reduces friction on Spark's own balance sheet, and a savings vault that could not be swept would strand idle capital. The controls that do bind here are the `Taker` role address (.9.1.4.1.4) and the supply cap, which caps the total that could ever be taken.

Seen from the depositor's side it is the sharpest asymmetry in the whole registry. Spark rate-limits itself when supplying capital to Aave or Maple — venues run by sophisticated counterparties — but not when drawing from its own retail depositors. The exposure is bounded by a cap set in the same document by the same process, rather than by an independent throttle, so the protection is entirely a governance promise rather than a mechanical one.
description: Every Spark Savings instance sets take and transferAssets maxAmount to Unlimited, so depositor protection rests on the supply cap and the Taker role rather than on any throttle.
